## 2026-11-15 — v0.65.1

### Fixed

- **Release notes cut from the changelog, and the ci-helpers vendor sync, no longer refuse it.** The 0.64.2 entry quoted an email-shaped example, which `check_sensitive.sh` blocks in release notes. It is reworded, and `make lint-docs` now runs `check_sensitive.sh --file CHANGELOG.md` so the next one fails in CI.

- **`check_sensitive.sh` no longer counts a CI runner's home as this machine's home directory in text.** On a GitHub runner `HOME` is `/home/runner`, so release notes naming `/home/runner` were refused by `check_publication.sh` and the 0.65.0 release step failed. The runner homes the binary check already skipped (`runner`, `runneradmin`, `github` under `/home`, `/Users` or `C:\Users`, and `/root`) are now skipped for every input; a personal home still blocks. Test: `test_ci_runner_home_in_text_is_not_a_machine_identifier` in `tests/scan_output_test.py`.

## 2026-11-14 — v0.65.0

### Upgrade notes

- **Behavior change: built binaries get a secrets-only check in `check_publication.sh`, and deb and rpm packages are decoded.** Files are sorted by magic bytes and validated headers: ELF, Mach-O, PE, AppImage, deb/ar, rpm, APK/AAB/JAR, dmg, and `<name>.split-NNN` parts; a decodable container is always decoded first. In a built binary, and in binary data inside a package, credentials (gitleaks), personal terms, machine identifiers and a local home path such as `/home/<name>/` still block; email, phone, SSN and card patterns and a CI runner's home path (`/home/runner`, `/Users/runner`) no longer do. Text members of a package keep every check, except license and documentation text (members named exactly `LICENSE`, `COPYING`, `NOTICE`, `COPYRIGHT`, `ThirdPartyNotices` and similar, or document formats under `usr/share/doc/` and `usr/share/licenses/`), where only email, phone, SSN and card patterns are skipped, and a deb `control` file's maintainer fields. A loose `LICENSE` file keeps every check. Before, every Flutter APK/AAB was refused for strings in `libflutter.so`, every Tauri AppImage exited 3 on Python older than 3.14 ("no zstd decoder"), Rust binaries were refused for the runner's `.cargo/registry` paths, and deb and rpm passed without their members being read. Undecodable data inside a built binary (squashfs, dmg, split parts, zstd without Python 3.14, 7z) gets a raw-bytes secrets check from the checker itself, in hooks and CI too, instead of exit 3; other undecodable data still exits 3, and a small `.zst` file without a decoder now exits 3 instead of passing unread. Each downgrade is named on stderr (`NOTICE: security policy:`), never with a value. New: `check_sensitive.sh --binary`, `check_scan_output.sh --classify` and `--strings`. Tests: `BinaryPolicyTests` in `tests/scan_output_test.py`.

### Fixed

- **`check_sensitive.sh --file` gives gitleaks the printable runs of a binary file too.** gitleaks skips a file it reads as binary, so a private key appended to an unrecognised binary passed. Test: new case in `tests/machine/publication_check.sh` (real gitleaks; fails without the fix).

## 2026-11-14 — v0.64.2

### Fixed

- **`check_scan_output.py` reads gzip files under the large-file limit instead of crashing.** `gzip.GzipFile` took the in-memory buffer as a filename and raised `TypeError`, so `check_publication.sh` refused every small `.tar.gz` or `.gz` (release tarballs included) whatever it held. bz2 and xz were not affected. Test: `test_small_compressed_files_are_read` in `tests/scan_output_test.py`.
- **A tarball inside a tarball is read instead of refused.** Every decompression and archive layer counts toward the nesting limit, so a `.tar.gz` inside a `.tar.gz` put its members at depth 4, past the limit of 3, and exited 2. The limit is 4; one level deeper still exits 2. Tests: `CompressedInputTests` in `tests/scan_output_test.py` (clean, planted token and address, nested, too deep, truncated and corrupt `.gz`/`.tar.gz`/`.tar.bz2`/`.tar.xz`).
- **`check_sensitive.sh` refuses binary noise as an email address less often.** 60 MB of random bytes held about one short email-shaped match (a 1-3 character name and short domain labels), so large binaries and compressed members were refused. A match with a local part of at most 3 characters and domain labels of at most 3 is skipped when every occurrence on its line has non-text bytes on both sides, ignoring one boundary byte at each end (a length prefix). Each skip is named on stderr. Longer addresses, and short ones beside text, are still refused. About 1 in 4 runs of 60 MB random data still hits (before: about 2 hits per run). Tests: `BinaryNoiseEmailTests` in `tests/scan_output_test.py`.
- **`check_sensitive.sh --file` and `--stdin` read text after a NUL byte on macOS.** NULs were stripped after awk labelled each line, and the macOS awk ends a record at a NUL, so the rest of that line (an address in a binary's string table, for one) was never checked. NULs are now stripped first. Tests: `test_text_after_a_nul_is_read`, and the NUL-separated case of `test_addresses_in_text_are_still_found`, which failed on the macOS leg, in `tests/scan_output_test.py`.
